thread:
mina: Heads up — after the proto framing change merged yesterday I'm seeing a consistent tail latency bump on SSE streams in staging (~+18ms P95). CI perf job also flagged a regression. Anyone else?

 tj: yeah saw that too. Repro with small payloads + toolcall enabled. Seems correlated with kernel-autoselect toggling.

 olga: can you paste a short log snippet?

 mina: pasted quick logs from reproduction run:
 ```
 [2026-03-17 21:12:34] stream: write 256 bytes -> flush delay 9ms
 [2026-03-17 21:12:34] kernel: selected cuda-kernel-v2 for seq_len 64
 [2026-03-17 21:12:34] proto: serialize took 12ms
 ```

 tj: interesting — the new proto framing coalesces header frames which increased flush coalescing window. Also saw an extra memcpy introduced in the kernel handoff. Those combined can push small-write streams over the latency SLO.

 deploy-bot: Deploy r-2026-03-17/nd starting canary (3 hosts) :rocket:

 olga: I ran a microbench with and without the merge:
 - baseline(master): p95 52ms
 - with merge: p95 71ms
 bench command:
 ```
 ./bench_stream --clients=20 --payload=small --seq=64 --toolcall=on
 ```

 mina: another thing I noticed — KV cache churn when toolcall frames arrive. It looks like cache keys changed shape after the merge (some requests miss now) which triggers kernel-autoselect fallback to a slower path on misses.

 ryan: on the kernel side autoselect prefers int8-optimized kernels when the cache hit pattern is stable. If misses happen it falls back to a safer float32 path which costs more. Why did the key change?

 tj: digging into the proto diff — we appended request_id into the cache key composition (previous key = model+seq+prefix, new key = model+seq+prefix+request_id). That makes most requests miss unless request_id is identical across retries.

 mina: confirmed locally — reverting request_id from the key returns cache hits and latency to baseline.

 perf-ci: CI perf job #7634 detected streaming P95 +29ms vs baseline (regression threshold exceeded).

 olga: options: revert the merge, make request_id opt-in, or only include request_id in analytics (not cache key). Thoughts?

 tj: propose hotfix: keep cache key stable (no request_id) in serving runtime; move request_id to separate analytics header. We should also add a flag to opt-in to request_id-based sharding if explicitly needed.

 mina: opened PR #3489 with hotfix and microbench results:
 - hotfix: p95 54ms
 - master(rebased + merge): p95 70ms

 tj: applying rollback on canary now.

 deploy-bot: Rollback applied to canary hosts — r-2026-03-17/nd rolled back on 3/3 hosts.

 ryan: follow-ups: 1) metric when kernel-autoselect falls back (so we can alert on fallback spikes), 2) metric for cache-hit-by-key-version, 3) unit tests asserting cache-key stability across minor proto changes.

 olga: +1. I'll open a follow-up GH issue to add metrics and tests. Also we should add a short note in the release checklist: do not change cache-key composition without perf sign-off.

 mina: thanks all — I'll merge the hotfix once CI clears and then re-run the full perf suite. :thumbsup:

 tj: assigning to eng-runtime oncall — @ryan can you take ownership?

 ryan: taking it. Will monitor canary perf and add the fallback metric in a follow-up.

 mina: closing the loop here — revert in canary restored p95 near-baseline. Will follow up with postmortem entry.

 olga: noted for postmortem.

 mina: end of thread.
